expectations.text: Defines a TypeScript TemplateSpec type/interface (e.g. extends Lightning.Component.TemplateSpec) rather than typing the whole class as any
expectations.evidence: Button.ts lines 9-19: `export interface ButtonTemplateSpec extends Lightning.Component.TemplateSpec { Background: { color: number }; Label: { text: { text: string; fontSize: number } }; }`. The class extends `Lightning.Component<ButtonTemplateSpec>` (line 25) and `static _template()` is annotated to return `Lightning.Component.Template<ButtonTemplateSpec>` (line 34), so the interface is actually wired into the class rather than being decorative. No `any` appears anywhere in the file (grep for `any` returned zero matches).

expectations.text: Template child refs (Background, Label) use PascalCase and are distinguished from camelCase properties (onEnter, label) per Lightning's TS conventions
expectations.evidence: Interface children `Background`/`Label` (Button.ts lines 10, 13) and the class's typed ref fields `readonly Background`/`readonly Label` (lines 31-32) are PascalCase, matching the original JS ref names (`this.tag('Background')`, `this.tag('Label')`). The component's own API surface, `set onEnter(cb)` (line 56) and `set label(value)` (line 60), stays camelCase. This mirrors the naming split documented in the skill's own reference/typescript.md ('Properties: lower-case keys... Children: upper-case keys').

expectations.text: The onEnter callback prop has a real function type (e.g. () => void), not any
expectations.evidence: Line 22: `export type ButtonOnEnterCallback = () => void;`. Applied to the private backing field (`private _onEnter: ButtonOnEnterCallback | null = null;`, line 28) and the setter parameter (`set onEnter(cb: ButtonOnEnterCallback | null)`, line 56) — a real, callable function type, not `any`.

expectations.text: Uses getByRef() (or another typed accessor) rather than untyped tag() calls for accessing typed children
expectations.evidence: Lines 31-32: `readonly Background = this.getByRef('Background')!;` and `readonly Label = this.getByRef('Label')!;`, then used at every access site (`this.Background.patch(...)` in `_focus`/`_unfocus`, `this.Label.patch(...)` in the `label` setter). A grep of the file for `tag(` found zero matches — every previous `this.tag('X')` call from the original JS was replaced.

claims.claim: The chosen `getByRef`/`ImplementTemplateSpec` pattern matches idiomatic Lightning TS usage
